title: Optimal Uncertainty Relations for a Single Observable
summary: Uncertainty relations are usually formulated as trade-offs between two or more observables. Yet the uncertainty of a single observable can already contain an intrinsically quantum contribution arising from its noncommutativity with the state. In the sense of Luo, such a contribution can be quantified by a quantum uncertainty $Q_ρ(A)$, with prominent examples including the Wigner--Yanase and Wigner--Yanase--Dyson skew informations and the quantum Fisher information. Here we ask how strong such single-observable uncertainty relations can be when the quantum state is fixed. We solve this…
